opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll, which is at the allowed maximum (write) for full-time employees in a system owned by their role. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds the allowed maximum, so recommend read. (Note: this conflicts with the prior note stating full_time; security record indicates contractor.)
reason: There is conflicting employment information: HR notes Daniel Gutierrez (E046) as full_time, while Security notes contractor with basic security training and explicitly states the security record indicates contractor. Under the contractor policy, a contractor with basic training maxes out at read; the requested write exceeds this maximum, so the maximum permitted level is granted. Granting read is also within the full-time policy, making it the safe level given the conflicting records.
